$comment: El Carot persists everything on-device via lib/storage.ts (AsyncStorage). On web AsyncStorage is backed by plain localStorage with no key prefix, so these keys map 1:1 to the localStorage keys the CodeYam seed adapter injects. Production starts empty — a fresh install has no daily card and no history.

tables.name: elcarot.dailyCard
tables.description: The card locked in for the current day. Absent until the user opens the daily screen for the first time that day.

fields.name: date
fields.description: Local calendar day the card belongs to, as YYYY-MM-DD. A stored date older than today means a fresh card is due.

fields.name: n
fields.description: Major-arcana index 0-21, keying into CAROT_CARDS in data/cards.ts.

fields.name: revealed
fields.description: Whether the user has already flipped the card face-up. Return visits the same day render the reveal directly when true.

tables.name: elcarot.history
tables.description: Past daily cards for the signed-out reader, newest first. A day is appended once its card is revealed. Empty array on a fresh install. When an account is signed in this key is left untouched and the scoped key below is read instead, so signing out restores exactly the trail that was there before.

tables.name: elcarot.history.<accountId>
tables.description: Past daily cards belonging to one signed-in account — same shape as elcarot.history, one key per account. The suffix is the account id from elcarot.session. Two people signing in on the same phone each get their own trail, and neither can see the other's.

tables.name: elcarot.dailyCard.<accountId>
tables.description: The current day's card for one signed-in account — same shape as elcarot.dailyCard, one key per account. Absent while signed out, when the unscoped key is used instead.

fields.name: date
fields.description: Local calendar day the card belongs to, as YYYY-MM-DD.

fields.name: revealed
fields.description: Whether the user has already flipped the card face-up.

tables.name: elcarot.session
tables.description: The account currently signed in, or absent when reading anonymously. Login is entirely optional in El Carot — the app is fully usable with this key missing, which is the production default on a fresh install. Written on a successful Apple or Google sign-in and removed on sign-out.

fields.name: provider
fields.description: 'apple' or 'google' — which button the reader signed in with.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Stable account identifier from the provider, namespaced by provider so an Apple and a Google account can never collide. Used as the suffix on the scoped history and daily-card keys.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Display name for the greeting. Null when the provider withheld it — Apple only returns the name on the very first authorization, and lets the user hide it entirely — so the greeting must fall back to the generic welcome rather than render an empty name.

fields.name: email
fields.description: Provider email, when shared. Null for Apple's private-relay users who declined to share it. Not displayed anywhere today; stored so an account stays recognisable if the name is withheld.

tables.name: elcarot.lang
tables.description: Persisted language preference for card text. Defaults to 'es' when absent.

tables.name: elcarot.todayOverride
tables.description: Test/scenario seam only — never written by the app. When present, the date helper treats this YYYY-MM-DD as today so scenarios can pin a specific day and stay reproducible across calendar dates.

fields.name: value
fields.description: A YYYY-MM-DD date to substitute for the real clock.
